measured_for: Macao SAR, all residential units with a lease in force (not only new lets), per m2 of usable area; all size bands
note: DSEC Rental Statistics Q3 2026: average rent MOP140 per m2 of usable area x 75 m2 = MOP10,500. Rents come from lease declarations for property tax filed with the Financial Services Bureau; the average covers every unit with an unexpired lease, so it lags the going rate for a new let. DSEC rents are per usable area, which is smaller than gross area, so 75 m2 usable is a large flat. Size bands in Q3: under 50 m2 MOP168, 100-149.9 m2 MOP129, 150+ m2 MOP124; the 50-99.9 m2 band was not in the release text (Q1 2026: MOP139, so about the same as the all-flat average). Districts: Doca do Lamau MOP154, Baixa de Macau 119, Barca 117, ZAPE 122, Areia Preta and Iao Hon 121. Q2 2026 was MOP140, Q1 2026 MOP140, year on year -0.1%.
quote: the average rent per square metre of usable area for residential units increased by 0.1% quarter-on-quarter to MOP140 in the third quarter of 2026

measured_for: Ulaanbaatar, six central districts, asking rent of 3-room (2 bedrooms plus living room) flats on unegui.mn
note: NSO experimental estimate for August 2026, as reported by iKon.mn; NSO's own release was not found online (its PxWeb API carries sale prices but no rent table). Asking rents from unegui.mn listings, six central districts only. Mongolians count the living room, so a 3-room (3 өрөө) flat is two bedrooms plus living room, the nearest match to a 70-85 m2 two-bedroom; this room-count reading and the typical size (one listing found was 66 m2) are not stated by NSO. 2-room (1 bedroom) average is 1,930,000 MNT, 1-room 1,400,000. Series for a 3-room flat: Dec 2025 3.06m, Feb 2026 3.01m, Jul 2026 2.95m, Aug 2026 3.03m. The iKon.mn headline says 2-room 1.85m, but its text says 1.93m (1.85m is February's figure), so the text is used. Sep 2026 and later not found. Highest: Sukhbaatar district (Sukhbaatar Square, 220 mingat) 3-room 4.9m; Bayangol 3-room 2.2m; Khan-Uul Zaisan/River Garden 3-room 4.06m.

measured_for: Chengdu, the five central districts (Jinjiang, Qingyang, Jinniu, Wuhou, Chenghua): unweighted mean of 58 subdistrict rents for residential flats (住宅类), per m2
note: Second row for Chengdu; the first is the CRIC row (2,365 yuan for a 60-90 m2 flat, whole city). This one is official: the Chengdu housing bureau publishes average rent by subdistrict each quarter in yuan per m2 per month, residential (住宅类), apartment (公寓类) and dormitory (宿舍类) separately. Unweighted mean of the 58 residential subdistrict figures in the five central districts is 33.49 yuan per m2 (median 33.63); x 75 m2 = 2,512 yuan. District means: Jinjiang 38.13, Wuhou 34.95, Chenghua 33.13, Qingyang 32.11, Jinniu 29.88. Chunxi Road subdistrict, the commercial centre: 43.76, x 75 = 3,282 yuan. All 183 subdistricts in the city: mean 23.13. The bureau's own page was not opened (its site refused the request with HTTP 412); the table is read from the Chengdu Bendibao reprint. The reprint does not say how the bureau measured it (asking or signed, building or usable area).
